finding.claim: OS command injection in GET /ping: the unauthenticated query parameter `host` is concatenated into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, which runs it via /bin/sh. An attacker can append shell metacharacters (e.g. `;`, `&&`, `$()`, backticks) to run arbitrary commands as the server user, and the command output is returned in the response.
finding.source: req.query.host (HTTP GET /ping?host=...), attacker-controlled, no authentication. Express listener on port 3001, with no host argument, so it binds on all interfaces.
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7. exec spawns a shell. The stdout is reflected via res.send(out) at tools.js:11.

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping, with no auth middleware
req.query.host is concatenated directly into the shell command string passed to exec()
Command stdout is returned to the caller, so output of injected commands is visible. This is an output-reflecting RCE. Example: /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id
app.listen(3001) with no host binds on all interfaces, so the route is reachable from the network

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allow-list or regex on host. No escaping. No authentication or authorization middleware (no app.use calls). No use of execFile or an argument array for this route (execFile is used only in /version, with a fixed argument array). No rate limiting. No loopback-only binding. Note: a failed ping returns 502 with no body, but injected commands that exit 0 still reflect output. A host beginning with `-` could also cause argument injection, but shell injection already subsumes it.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec (shell) in an unauthenticated route (tools.js:6) with no validation or middleware, and tools.js:11 reflects stdout, with tools.js:28 listening on all interfaces.
